title: Shared pending TTS set can drop tasks created while waiting
reasoning: The pipeline stores pending TTS tasks in an instance-level set, then wait_for_pending_tts snapshots the current set, awaits only that snapshot, and unconditionally clears the whole set. If the same StreamPipeline instance processes another event while wait_for_pending_tts is awaiting, the new task can be added to _pending_tts_tasks after the snapshot and then removed by clear() without being awaited. A subsequent flush could therefore run before that TTS chunk finishes, reintroducing the audio-loss race this tracking is meant to prevent. The class comments also say all per-stream state should live outside the pipeline, but this set is pipeline-owned shared state.
recommendation: Move pending TTS tracking to a per-stream processor/context, or make wait_for_pending_tts remove only the tasks it actually awaited, for example by discarding the snapshot tasks instead of clearing the entire shared set. If StreamPipeline is intended to be per-query, enforce that lifecycle at construction/use sites and document it in the contract.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for concurrent calls or for tasks added while wait_for_pending_tts is awaiting.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a fake TTS processor whose first task blocks, call wait_for_pending_tts, then call process again before the first task completes. Assert the second task remains pending or is awaited before flush is allowed.
